page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for compute-intensive workloads. It features 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 192 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 12 GB of RAM per core. Graphics and parallel processing acceleration are delivered via a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which includes 48 GB of dedicated VRAM.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in several categories. The single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores, along with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, rank in the top 10%. Image processing and text processing benchmarks also achieve top-tier status. For large-block memory bandwidth, both read and write operations rank in the top 25%. In LLM inference tests, the server achieves top-tier speeds for prompt processing and text generation with a small 135M model, while maintaining strong to average performance on larger 7B and 70B models.

A primary hardware tradeoff is the lack of local storage, as the instance lists local storage as none. Additionally, the CPU allocation is shared, which may introduce performance variability compared to dedicated cores. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density of 12 GB per core combined with a professional-grade 48 GB GPU offers a resource-dense profile for memory-heavy and GPU-accelerated tasks without requiring a higher vCPU count.

This server configuration is highly suitable for machine learning inference, particularly for small to medium-sized language models, image processing, and data science tasks. The combination of 192 GB of system RAM and 48 GB of GPU VRAM also makes it appropriate for database operations, rendering, and memory-intensive parallel computing workloads.
description: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server featuring 16 shared AMD EPYC 9575F vCPUs, 192 GB of system memory, and a single NVIDIA L40S GPU with 48 GB of VRAM. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization, this instance delivers top-tier single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as evidenced by Geekbench and stress-ng benchmarks. It also demonstrates strong large-block memory bandwidth and top-tier performance in image processing and small-model LLM inference. A notable hardware tradeoff is the absence of local storage and the shared nature of the CPU allocation. This configuration is highly efficient for memory-intensive parallel processing, machine learning inference, and data science workloads that require substantial GPU memory without a massive vCPU footprint.
